 THIS CRL.A. IS FILED U/S.378(1) AND (3) OF CR.P.C.
PRAYING TO GRANT LEAVE TO FILE AN APPEAL AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND ORDER OF ACQUITTAL DATED 23.12.2016 PASSED BY THE I ADDL. DIST. AND S.J., CHITRADURGA IN S.C.NO.101/2015 THEREBY ACQUITTING THE RESPONDENT/ACCUSED FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 498(A)
AND 304(B) R/W 34 OF IPC.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
VIJAYKUMAR A. PATIL J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed by the State questioning the correctness of the judgment of acquittal dated 23.12.2016 passed by the I Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Chitradurga in S.C.No.101/2015.

entities.text: I Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Chitradurga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Facts in brief leading to filing of this appeal are that the marriage between deceased and accused No.1 was solemnized on 15.08.2014.
The family of the deceased paid Rs.1,00,000/- and a gold ring as dowry to the accused.
The accused No.1 and the deceased started residing at Chitradurga.
The accused Nos.1 to 3 and 6 are the husband and in-laws of the deceased.

They caused torture,
instigated the deceased Smt.Nagarathnamma to bring Rs.1,00,000/- from her parents' house,
thereby made her to commit suicide by hanging herself on 01.06.2015 in the bedroom of the matrimonial home.
It is the case of prosecution that the accused No.1 started screaming.

On hearing, PW-8 Ravikumar, PW-10 Thippakka and others rushed to the house of accused No.1, broke open the room door, alighted Smt.Nagarathnamma and shifted her to District Hospital, Chitradurga where the doctor declared her dead.
The accused No.1 telephonically informed PW-1, father of the deceased that Nagarathnamma committed suicide.
PW-1 gave information of the incident to the police.

A case was NC: 2024:KHC:6279-DB registered against the accused persons in Crime State Of Karnataka vs Varadaraj on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23891848/
2 No.243/2015.
3.

entities.text: Crime State Of Karnataka vs Varadaraj on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The investigating officer, after completion of investigation filed charge sheet against accused Nos.1 to 6 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 304B read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
The Trial Court framed charges against accused Nos.1 to 3 and 6 for the aforesaid offences.
The Trial Court vide order dated 10.05.2016 discharged accused Nos.4 and 5 from the accusation of offences.

4. The prosecution, in order to prove the guilt of the accused examined 24 witnesses as PWs-1 to 24,
got marked 31 documents as Exs.P1 to P31 and 6 material objects as MOs-1 to 6.

The Trial Court, on appreciation of the evidence on record came to the conclusion that the evidence of PWs- 1, 4, 12 and 13, parents, brother and sister of the deceased does not corroborate the contents of the complaint and the statements made by them before the police.

It is further observed that with regard to the payment of Rs.1,00,000/- by PW-1 to the accused No.1 at the time of marriage, the evidence of PWs-1, 4, 12 and 13 also does not find corroboration from the evidence of other witnesses.
The neighbours of the house of the accused did not support the case of the prosecution with regard to the alleged torture to the victim by the accused.

The Trial Court recorded a finding that the allegations made against the accused by the family members of the deceased are inconsistent with complaint, statement and further statement and there are a lot of improvement with regard to the alleged torture.
Hence, it cannot be believed.

The Trial Court has come to the conclusion that on perusal of the entire evidence a doubt has been created in the mind of the Court with regard to inflicting cruelty on the deceased and demand of dowry.
The Trial Court granted the benefit of doubt in favour of the accused and proceeded to acquit the accused from the charged offences.
Hence, this appeal.
6. We have heard Sri.B.N.Jagadish, Addl.

State Public Prosecutor for the appellant - State,
Sri.Hashmath NC: 2024:KHC:6279-DB Pasha, learned Senior counsel for Sri.Kariappa, learned counsel for the respondents.
7.
Sri.B.N.Jagadish, learned Addl. State Public Prosecutor argues that the Trial Court committed a grave error in appreciating the evidence adduced by the prosecution.
The Trial Court failed to take note of the fact that the deceased made complaints about cruelty to her parents, brother and sister whenever she visited her parents' house.

The evidence on record also indicates that whenever the deceased made a telephone call, she made complaints that the accused No.1 has bad habits of consuming alcohol, gambling and adultery, etc. which clearly goes to show that the accused No.1 used to cause cruelty against the deceased on the ground of demand of dowry.

It is submitted that the Trial Court failed to consider that the death of victim is unnatural and has taken place within 7 years of her marriage that too in the house of accused and preceding conduct of the accused No.1 and other family members discloses that the accused caused cruelty on the deceased by demanding dowry which establishes the guilt of the NC: 2024:KHC:6279-DB accused.

It is further submitted that the Trial Court has given much weightage to the minor contradictions in the evidence of family State Of Karnataka vs Varadaraj on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23891848/
3 members.

entities.text: family State Of Karnataka vs Varadaraj on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that if the entire evidence adduced by the prosecution is perused, the ingredients of offences under Sections 498A, 304B and 34 are established.
The Trial Court failed to appreciate the evidence of PWs-14 and 16, the independent witnesses who had participated in the marriage negotiations.

The other family members clearly stated that there was a demand for dowry,
and the consequent cruelty on the deceased.
These facts have not been properly appreciated by the Trial Court which resulted in acquittal of the accused from the charged offences.
He seeks to reverse the judgment of acquittal by convicting the accused and punishing them appropriately.
8. Per contra, Sri.Hashmath Pasha, learned Senior counsel for the respondents-accused submits that the prosecution failed to prove the demand for dowry and also failed to prove the cruelty aspect.
The father of the deceased PW-1 neither stated anything with regard to demand for dowry nor spoke with regard to cruelty.
He stated that his NC: 2024:KHC:6279-DB daughter used to tell him that accused No.1 was having bad habits.
It is submitted that in the complaint at Ex.P2 there is no whisper with regard to demand for dowry or cruelty by the accused.

He submits that the complaint being the initial document of investigation, clearly demonstrates that there is no demand for dowry,
payment of dowry or the cruelty on the part of accused.
It is further submitted that the Executive Magistrate conducted inquest on the dead body as per Ex.P4.
The Executive Magistrate recorded the statement of witnesses including PW-1. who did not state anything with regard to demand for dowry, payment of dowry or cruelty by the accused.
PW-1 stated that a gold ring was given to accused at the time of marriage, but it was a customary.
9. Learned senior counsel for the respondents further argues that there was a matrimonial discord between the accused No.1 and deceased, hence deceased committed suicide.
He submits that on perusal of entire evidence of prosecution, the ingredients of Sections 498A, 304B and 34 of IPC are not found.
All the prosecution witnesses have NC: 2024:KHC:6279-DB spoken with regard to the incident, however there is no evidence on record that the accused caused cruelty for demand for dowry.

He further argues that PW-4 the mother of the deceased stated that her daughter informed her that accused No.1 had indulged in bad habits viz., consuming alcohol, gambling and having illicit relationship with other woman.
She has not spoken anything with regard to demand for dowry or cruelty.

He also argues that PWs-12 & 13, i.e., younger brother and sister of the deceased, have spoken about giving dowry of Rs.1,00,000/- to accused No.1 which is not corroborated by the evidence of PWs-1 & 4 and the complaint at Ex.P-2, hence their evidence is rightly disbelieved by Trial Court.
He submits that the prosecution examined neighbours i.e., PWs-7 to 11 who have not supported the case of prosecution.
None of the independent witnesses has spoken about the cruelty and demand for dowry.

He refers to the evidence of PWs-14 & 16 who claim that they had participated in the marriage negotiations and also had about the payment of dowry, however the father and mother of deceased themselves have not stated anything - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:6279-DB about demand for dowry.
Hence, the question of believing their evidence would not arise.
Therefore, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.

4 10.

sentences.text: We have heard the learned Additional State Public Prosecutor for the appellant-State, learned Senior counsel for the respondents-accused, perused the impugned judgment of the Trial Court and the entire evidence available on record.
Now we re-appreciate the evidence available on record.
11. PW-1 is the father of deceased.
He stated with regard to the solemnization of marriage between accused No.1 and the deceased.
He also stated that they gave one gold ring to accused No.1.

He stated that accused No.1 and deceased have led their marital life happily for a period of four months and thereafter the deceased used to complain that accused No.1 is addicted to consuming alcohol,
gambling and adultery.

The said habits of accused No.1 was brought to the notice of his parents i.e.,
accused Nos.2 & 3, but they inturn informed that accused No.1 is not listening - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:6279-DB to their words.
PW-1 further stated that the deceased used to make telephone calls and inform that accused No.1 is torturing her and assaulting her.

He stated that the deceased came to their house after quarreling with accused No.1 during the time of Kanive Maramma festival and she informed that accused No.1 quarrelled with her and after the festival,
PW-1 took the deceased to matrimonial home
. At that time, accused No.1 questioned PW-1 as to why the deceased was brought back to matrimonial home, as he wanted to give divorce to her.

Then,
accused No.2 intervened and requested to leave the deceased in the matrimonial home and assured that he would take care of his daughter-in-law.
On such assurance, PW-1 left the deceased at the matrimonial home and came back.

He stated that after about a month, accused No.1 telephonically called and informed him that his wife had committed suicide by hanging herself in the room and they had taken her to Chitradurga District Hospital.
Thereafter, they went to the hospital and found that his daughter was dead and he gave information to police which was recorded at Ex.P2.
He - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:6279-DB further stated that the contents of Ex.P2 are not known to him and he does not know what has been written by the police and the Tahasildar.
12. PW-4 is the mother of deceased, she deposed in the lines of PW-1 with regard to performance of marriage, habits of accused No.1 and death of her daughter.
She stated that the police and Tahsildar have written contrary to what she had deposed.
She stated that she and her husband had given the complaint to police stating that accused had killed her daughter.
13. PW-12 is the brother of the deceased, he stated that his sister was given in marriage to accused No.1 and at the time of marriage they gave Rs.1,00,000/- as dowry.

He stated that in the initial days,
accused No.1 and deceased led married life happily and thereafter accused No.1 caused cruelty on the deceased by stating that he was not interested in seeing the face of deceased, she was not a good looking woman and not interested to lead married life with her.

He stated that deceased informed him that accused No.1 - 13 - State Of Karnataka vs Varadaraj on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23891848/
5 NC: 2024:KHC:6279-DB insisted to bring Rs.1,00,000/- from her parents and he used to assault and cause cruelty to her.

Similarly, PW-13, who is the sister of the deceased, has stated that deceased came to her parents house after quarrelling with accused No.1 and informed that accused No.1 was inflicting cruelty, addicted to bad habits and demanding money.
She stated that the deceased had called her on 01.06.2015 around 11.00 a.m. and informed that she wish to see her child.

However,
she informed that she would come next day to her matrimonial home along with children, but on the same day around 04.30 p.m. her father called and informed about the death of her sister.
14. PWs-14 and 16 are the persons who participated in the marriage negotiations of the deceased and accused No.1.
PW-14 stated that PW-1 agreed to give one gold ring, gold chain and Rs.1,00,000/- to the accused No.1 at the time of marriage.
Similarly, PW-16 stated that one gold ring, gold chain and Rs.1,00,000/- was given to the accused No.1 at the time of marriage.

He further stated that initially for a period of three months the accused No.1 and deceased led - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:6279-DB married life happily and deceased telephonically informed him one day that the accused No.1 was insisting her to bring dowry. PW-15 stated that he participated in the marriage negotiations, however, did not speak anything with regard to the terms of negotiation.
15. PWs-17 to 19 turned hostile.
They are the witnesses who participated in the marriage negotiations.
PW-20 stated that PW-1 borrowed Rs.50,000/- loan from him for the purpose of performing the marriage.
PW-21 turned hostile.
He stated that he did not give any loan to PW-1.
PWs-22 to 24 are the official witnesses who spoke with regard to receipt of information, registration of FIR and manner of conducting investigation.
16. PW-5 is the Taluka Executive Magistrate who conducted the inquest on the dead body.
He recorded the statements of PWs-1 and 4.
PW-5 stated that at the request of the police, he conducted inquest on 02.06.2015 between 7.15 a.m. and 9.15 a.m.
He further stated that he recorded - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:6279-DB the statements of PW-1 Rajamma PW-2, Rajesh and Chandrappa PW-3.

The said inquest is marked as Ex.P4.
17.

After re-appreciation of the entire evidence available on record, it is emerged that PW-1 father of the deceased, PW-4 mother of the deceased have spoken with regard to the performance of marriage of their daughter with the accused No.1.
They have spoken with regard to the information received from accused No.1 telephonically that their daughter had committed suicide.

They have also spoken that the deceased used to complain to them with regard to the bad habits of the accused No.1 i.e.
addiction of alcohol, gambling and leading adulteress life and also that he was causing cruelty to her.
In the cross-examination, PW-1 stated that they gave one gold ring to the accused No.1 at the time of marriage.
They have also spoken with regard to the incident which took place between the accused No.1 and the deceased during Kanive Maramma festival.

On perusal of the entire evidence State Of Karnataka vs Varadaraj on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23891848/
6 of PWs-1 and 4, it is very much clear that there is no allegation of demand of dowry by the accused and payment of dowry.

entities.text: State Of Karnataka vs Varadaraj on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Giving of one gold ring - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC:6279-DB during marriage is a customary practice.
PW-1 who is the informant to the police as per Ex.P2, did not state anything with regard to the demand of dowry by the accused No.1 and causing cruelty for non-payment of such dowry.

In the absence of any such evidence on record,
it can be fairly concluded that there was no demand for dowry from the accused No.1.
PW-5 the Executive Magistrate recorded the statement of PW-1 at the time of conducting inquest.
On perusal of the said statement at Ex.P4, it is evident that PW- 1 did not speak anything with regard to demand and payment of dowry to the accused.
On close scrutiny of the evidence of PWs-1 and 4, father and mother of the deceased, what emerges is that there was marital discord between the accused No.1 and the deceased.
18. The evidence of PWs-12 and 13, brother and sister of the deceased is quite contrary to the evidence of PWs-1 and 4.
These two witnesses spoke with regard to the demand of dowry.

However,
such statement of demand of dowry is not corroborated by the evidence of any other witness.
The prosecution failed to establish a link between - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC:6279-DB unnatural death, cruelty and demand of dowry.

The evidence of PWs-12 and 13 is not trustworthy for the simple reason that the other witnesses i.e. the neighbours who participated in the marriage negotiations, have not supported the case of prosecution.
None of the witnesses has spoken about cruelty and demand for dowry.

The evidence on record clearly establishes that the deceased hanged herself in a room which was locked and the accused No.1 seeing the incident screamed and neighbours gathered there, broke open the door, alighted the body of the deceased and accused took her to the hospital.
Immediately, accused No.1 called PW-1 and informed him about suicide.
If the narration of events is to be seen, it can fairly be concluded that the accused No.1 is not responsible for the unnatural death of deceased Nagarathnamma.
There is absolutely no evidence available on record with regard to the other accused insofar as demand for dowry and cruelty.
PW-1 in his evidence, clearly stated that his daughter came to his house and informed that there was a quarrel between her and the accused No.1.
The quarrel between the accused - 18 - NC: 2024:KHC:6279-DB No.1 and the deceased was routine marital discord and nothing relating to demand for dowry.

The evidence of PW-1 is that after the festival when he took his daughter to the matrimonial home, the accused No.1 questioned him as to why the deceased came back to the matrimonial home as he intended to give divorce to her.

At that time, accused No.2 the father of the accused No.1 intervened and told PW-1 to leave his daughter in the matrimonial home and if the accused No.1 failed to take care of her, he would take care of her.

This evidence of PW-1 clearly State Of Karnataka vs Varadaraj on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23891848/
7 establishes that there is no role of the other accused with regard to unnatural death of the deceased.
19. PWs-14 and 16 are the persons who participated in the marriage negotiations, who stated that PW-1 gave one ring, one chain and Rs.1,00,000/- at the time of marriage.
PW-16 stated that deceased called him and informed that the accused No.1 is demanding Rs.1,00,000/- and causing cruelty.

The aforesaid witnesses are not trustworthy to be believed for the simple reason that PWs-1 and 4, the parents of the deceased did not state anything with regard to - 19 - NC: 2024:KHC:6279-DB payment of Rs.1,00,000/- at the time of marriage.
Hence, these witnesses who are outsiders, cannot have knowledge of payment of dowry.
Their evidence is nothing but an exaggeration.

20. The material witnesses examined by the prosecution do not establish that the accused demanded dowry and the family members of the deceased had paid the dowry at the time of marriage and thereafter, there is no cogent and acceptable evidence on record which shows that the deceased was treated with cruelty resulting in her unnatural death.
The witnesses who have participated in the marriage negotiations have not fully supported the case of prosecution.
The Trial Court has rightly noticed and recorded that there are a number of contradictions between the evidence of PWs-1, 4, 12 and 13.
Similarly, there are contradictions between the statements of PWs-1 and 4 and other witnesses with regard to demand and payment of dowry and cruelty.

We are of the considered view that the Trial Court, on appreciation of the entire evidence has recorded the finding that the prosecution has failed to prove - 20 - NC: 2024:KHC:6279-DB the case beyond reasonable doubt.

The aforesaid finding of the Trial Court is neither perverse nor contrary to the evidence available on record calling for interference in the appeal filed by the State against the impugned judgment of acquittal.
21. For the aforementioned reasons, we do not find any merit in this appeal.
Accordingly, the same is dismissed.
